cover.note: Leprévost 1995, §3.2: the degree-3 map X = (x-1)^2/(2x^3-15x^2-3) onto E1: Y^2 = 648X^3 + 297X^2 + 18X + 1 (54b3), written on the even model y^2 = 4f

reference: F. Leprévost, Jacobiennes de certaines courbes de genre 2: torsion et simplicité, J. Théor. Nombres Bordeaux 7 (1995), 283–306, https://doi.org/10.5802/jtnb.144: the curve C27 of Théorème 1.2.1 (p. 293), y^2 = (2x^3 - 15x^2 - 3)(2x^3 - 15x^2 + 12x - 3); §3.2 (p. 302) gives the explicit degree-3 cover onto E1 and shows that its Jacobian is not simple over Q. Not in the production LMFDB.
notes: Q-split witness for [27]: the census has only a geometrically simple curve and a Q-simple geometrically split curve (27.b) with this torsion group. Not a new curve: this is Leprévost's C27 (f above is (2x^3 - 15x^2 - 3)(2x^3 - 15x^2 + 12x - 3) expanded). It is not the census curve 27.b (different G2-invariants). Output of pipeline/magma/prepare_submission.m (Magma V2.29-4): J(Q)_tors = [27]; gcd of #J(F_p) over 25 good primes = 27 (sharp); no strict prime below 500; conductor (Magma, Ogg's formula at 2) 8748 = 2^2 * 3^7.
